subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should OpenClaw support explicit provider/model overrides for main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs, and should the public contract be `payload.model`, top-level cron fields, or a `sessionOverride` block?
rationale: Current code intentionally treats system events as text-only main-session injections, and enabling model overrides crosses provider routing, session state, cron persistence, UI/CLI, docs, and heartbeat semantics.

options.title: Design explicit override contract
options.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both main-session wake modes isolate state correctly.

options.title: Keep systemEvent text-only
options.body: Document this path as unsupported and steer cheap scheduled model calls to isolated/current/custom-session `agentTurn` jobs.

options.title: Defer to broader cron API work
options.body: Track the model decision with broader cron schema and cost-control work so model, context, timeout, and spend semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Design explicit override contract
recommendation.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both main-session wake modes isolate state correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron runtime/schema work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the API and session-state decision.
